note: Public amendment records. research_notes are deliberately absent from this file; unpublished notes live in research-private/ and are never deployed. verification_status values: VERIFIED (primary source confirms), PARTIALLY_VERIFIED (some evidence, one part missing), RESEARCH_NEEDED (evidence not yet located).

records.title: Qualifications for office
records.old_text_described: Reported that the charter required a candidate to be a U.S. citizen and qualified, without an express voter registration requirement.
records.new_text_described: Proposed: a candidate must be 18 years of age on the first day of the term to be filled or on the date of appointment, be registered to vote by the regular filing deadline, and have resided continuously inside the city limits for the 12 months immediately preceding the regular filing deadline or the date of appointment.
records.plain_language_summary: This sets the rules for who is allowed to run for city office. It adds a requirement that a candidate must already be a registered voter, and that they must have lived inside the city limits for a full year before signing up to run.
records.resident_effect: A resident who recently moved into the city, or who moved across the city limit line, could be blocked from running for office for up to a year.
records.government_effect: Narrows the pool of eligible candidates for council and mayor.
records.missing: Ballot outcome. Old and new charter text.

records.title: Compensation of council members
records.old_text_described: Mayor received $50 for each regular and special meeting attended. Council members received $25.
records.new_text_described: Proposed: mayor to $75 per meeting, council members to $50 per meeting.
records.plain_language_summary: This would have raised the amount the mayor and council members are paid for each meeting they attend. Voters said no.
records.resident_effect: No change. Council pay stayed where it was because residents rejected the increase.
records.government_effect: None. The increase did not take effect.
records.missing: Vote totals. The rejection is reported in later coverage, not yet confirmed against the canvass.

records.title: Hearings on forfeiture of office
records.old_text_described: Reported that requirements for holding a hearing on an alleged forfeiture of office were less specific.
records.new_text_described: Proposed: clarified the requirements for holding a forfeiture of office hearing.
records.plain_language_summary: Forfeiture of office is a way a sitting official can lose their seat without a recall election, usually for something like missing too many meetings or breaking a rule in the charter. This changed the process for holding that hearing.
records.resident_effect: Depends entirely on the actual wording. A clearer process can make removal more reliable, or it can add steps that make removal harder. The text is needed before anyone can say which.
records.government_effect: Changes the procedure by which the council handles an alleged forfeiture by one of its own members.
records.missing: Ballot outcome. Old and new charter text. This one is a research priority.

records.title: Remove unnecessary language
records.old_text_described: Charter contained Sec. 11.05 employee relations, Sec. 11.06 damage suits, Sec. 11.11 provisions relating to assignment, execution and garnishment, and Sec. 11.12 power to remit penalties. Sec. 2.09 governed meetings of the council.
records.new_text_described: Proposed: delete Sections 11.05, 11.06, 11.11 and 11.12, and revise Section 2.09, described by the committee as creating a more clear and simple home rule charter.
records.plain_language_summary: This removed four sections from the charter and rewrote the section about council meetings.
records.resident_effect: Section 2.09 controls when and how the council meets, which is when residents get to show up and speak. Whether this helped or hurt depends on what the rewrite says. Four deleted sections also need to be read before calling this cleanup.
records.government_effect: Shortens the charter. Effect on council meeting practice is unknown without the text.
records.missing: Ballot outcome. The deleted text of all four sections. The old and new Sec. 2.09.
records.corroboration: Corroborating evidence: Sections 11.05, 11.06, 11.11 and 11.12 are all Reserved in the current charter, and Sec. 2.09 Meetings of council still exists. That is exactly the outcome Measure D proposed. This raises confidence that Measure D was approved but does not establish it, because a section can be reserved by an earlier repeal or by renumbering. The canvass is still required.

records.title: Consistency with state law
records.old_text_described: Sec. 3.03 official ballots and Sec. 3.04 elections carried their own local requirements. Sec. 10.09 required submission of annual reports.
records.new_text_described: Proposed: Sec. 3.03 to read that official ballots shall be prepared consistent with the requirements of state law, Sec. 3.04 revised to be consistent with state law, and Sec. 10.09 eliminated.
records.plain_language_summary: This replaced the city's own election rules with a pointer to state law, and deleted a requirement that the city submit annual reports.
records.resident_effect: When a local rule is replaced by a pointer to state law, the rule can then change in Austin without a Copperas Cove vote. Deleting an annual reporting requirement removes a document residents could have relied on.
records.government_effect: Reduces the number of local requirements the city must satisfy beyond state law.
records.missing: Ballot outcome. The deleted Sec. 10.09 text. The prior Sec. 3.03 and 3.04.
records.corroboration: Corroborating evidence: Sec. 10.09 does not appear in the current charter at all, and Article X runs 10.01, 10.02, 10.10, 10.11. Sections 3.03 Official ballots and 3.04 Elections both still exist, consistent with revision rather than deletion. This is what Measure E proposed. The canvass is still required.

records.title: Petition signature requirements
records.old_text_described: Reported that a signer of an initiative or referendum petition had to provide both a date of birth and a voter registration number.
records.new_text_described: Ballot language: an amendment to the city's home rule charter requiring signers to an initiative or referendum petition to include either their date of birth or voter registration number but not require both.
records.plain_language_summary: When residents sign a petition to put something on the ballot, they now have to write down one identifying detail instead of two.
records.resident_effect: Appears to make petitions easier to sign and harder to throw out over a missing detail. This is the clearest candidate on the 2021 ballot for an increase in resident power, but the outcome still needs confirming.
records.government_effect: Fewer grounds for rejecting a signature during petition review.
records.missing: Ballot outcome. The signature count threshold itself, which this measure did not touch.

records.title: Non-substantive revisions
records.old_text_described: Charter contained Sec. 8.03, plus assorted grammar, gender and title references throughout.
records.new_text_described: Ballot language: an amendment to make non-substantive corrections, deletions and revisions to grammar, typographical errors, capitalization, punctuation, gender and title references, redundant provisions, and sentence and charter structure. The committee description also states it eliminates Sec. 8.03.
records.plain_language_summary: This was presented as a cleanup of spelling, grammar and outdated wording. It also removed one whole section.
records.resident_effect: Unknown until Sec. 8.03 is read. A measure labeled non-substantive that deletes an entire section deserves a look at what that section said.
records.missing: Ballot outcome. The text of the deleted Sec. 8.03.
records.corroboration: Corroborating evidence: Sec. 8.03 is Reserved in the current charter, which is the outcome Measure G proposed. Same caveat as Measure D. The canvass is still required, and the repealed text of 8.03 is still unknown.

records.title: City manager authorized absences from city council meetings
records.old_text_described: Reported that the city manager was required to attend council meetings.
records.new_text_described: Ballot language: an amendment allowing the city manager to miss a city council meeting when such absence is approved by city council.
records.plain_language_summary: The city manager can now skip a council meeting if the council agrees to it.
records.resident_effect: The top unelected administrator does not have to be in the room on nights the council approves an absence. That is one fewer person available to answer a resident question at a meeting.
records.government_effect: Gives the council discretion to excuse the city manager from attendance.
records.missing: Ballot outcome. The prior attendance requirement text.

records.title: Capital improvement plan reviewed annually
records.old_text_described: Reported that the capital improvement plan was reviewed every five years.
records.plain_language_summary: The city's long-range plan for building and fixing things gets looked at every year instead of every five years.
records.resident_effect: More frequent review generally means more frequent public documents about what the city plans to build and borrow for.
records.government_effect: Increases the frequency of a required planning review.
records.missing: Ballot outcome. Charter section number and text.

records.title: Capital outlay plan prepared and submitted annually
records.old_text_described: Reported that the capital outlay plan was prepared and submitted every five years.
records.plain_language_summary: The city's plan for major purchases gets prepared every year instead of every five years.
records.resident_effect: Annual spending plans are easier to follow than five-year ones.
records.government_effect: Increases the frequency of a required submission.
records.missing: Ballot outcome. Charter section number and text.

records.title: Personnel plan prepared and submitted annually
records.old_text_described: Reported that a personnel plan was prepared and submitted every five years.
records.plain_language_summary: The plan covering city staffing gets prepared every year instead of every five years.
records.resident_effect: More frequent public documents about city staffing.
records.government_effect: Increases the frequency of a required submission by the administration.
records.missing: Ballot outcome. Charter section number and text.

records.title: Cosigner, director of budget
records.old_text_described: Reported that city checks were countersigned by the assistant director of finance.
records.new_text_described: Proposed: all checks countersigned by the director of budget rather than the assistant director of finance.
records.plain_language_summary: The second signature required on city checks moved from one staff position to another.
records.resident_effect: Who signs off on city money is a financial control question. The practical effect depends on which position sits closer to the spending decision.
records.government_effect: Moves a financial control duty between administrative positions.
records.missing: Ballot outcome. Charter section number and text.

records.title: Public officials and employees comply with state law
records.old_text_described: Sec. 11.02 conflict of interest carried the city's own definitions and prohibitions.
records.new_text_described: Proposed revision to Sec. 11.02: for purposes of this section the term City Official means any individual subject to the requirements of Texas Local Government Code Chapter 171. It is prohibited for members of city council or a city official to violate the rules and regulations regarding conflicts of interest as set out in Texas Local Government Code Chapter 171.
records.plain_language_summary: The city's own conflict of interest rule was replaced with the state's rule.
records.resident_effect: If the old local rule was stricter than the state rule, the ethics standard went down. If the old rule was weaker or unenforceable, it went up. The old Sec. 11.02 text is what decides this, and it has not been located.
records.government_effect: Aligns the city conflict of interest standard with Chapter 171.
records.missing: Ballot outcome. The prior Sec. 11.02 text. This determines whether the ethics standard rose or fell.
records.corroboration: Corroborating evidence: Sec. 11.02 Conflict of interest still exists in the current charter, consistent with revision rather than deletion. The prior text remains unknown, so whether the ethics standard rose or fell is still undetermined.

records.title: Compensation of the mayor and council members
records.old_text_described: Council members receive $25 for each regular and special meeting attended. Mayor receives $50.
records.new_text_described: Proposed: council members to $75 per meeting, mayor to $100 per meeting. Rejected, so the prior amounts remain.
records.plain_language_summary: This would have raised meeting pay for the mayor and council. Residents voted it down for the second time in two years.
records.resident_effect: No change to the charter. Council pay is one of the few things the council cannot change without asking residents first.
records.government_effect: None. The increase did not take effect.
records.missing: Official canvass confirming the reported totals of 960 for and 1,393 against.

records.title: Strike language inconsistent with state law
records.old_text_described: Charter carried language in various sections that conflicted with state law.
records.new_text_described: Reported: strikes language from various sections that is inconsistent with state law.
records.plain_language_summary: Conflicting wording was taken out of the charter. State law already controlled in those spots, so this mostly changed the document rather than the rule.
records.resident_effect: Likely minimal, but which sections were touched has not been confirmed.
records.government_effect: Removes charter language that could not be enforced anyway.
records.missing: Vote totals. Which sections were struck.
